# Reference set + domain-specific patterns (moved from SKILL.md, 2026-08-25 — context tax; content unchanged)

## Recommended reference set

The canonical short list. Keep these handy.

1. **Rougier, Droettboom, Bourne (2014).** "Ten Simple Rules for Better Figures." *PLOS Computational Biology* 10(9): e1003833. Open access, foundational, 10 minutes to read. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003833
2. **Wong, Bang.** *Points of View* column, *Nature Methods*, 2010-2013. Forty short essays each on one design principle (color, design, points, layouts, typography, salience). Wong's 8-color colorblind-safe palette (2011) is the de-facto standard.
3. **Altman & Krzywinski.** *Points of Significance* and *Points of View* columns, *Nature Methods*, 2013-present. Statistical visualization, error bars, distributions, flow.
4. **Tufte, Edward.** *The Visual Display of Quantitative Information* (1983, 2nd ed. 2001). The data-ink ratio principle.
5. **Cairo, Alberto.** *The Truthful Art* (2016). Modern follow-up; particularly good on hierarchy and color.
6. **Brewer, Cynthia.** ColorBrewer 2.0. https://colorbrewer2.org/
7. **AAAS Science Figure Standards.** https://www.science.org/content/page/instructions-preparing-initial-manuscript
8. **Nature Neuroscience Author Guidelines.** https://www.nature.com/neuro/submission-guidelines/
9. **Allen Brain Atlas.** https://atlas.brain-map.org/
10. **Marx, V. (2013).** "Drawing biology with neural circuit diagrams." *Nature Methods* 10, 939.

---


## Neuroscience-only patterns (4.1-4.2)

**4.1 Schematic neuron / cognitive cell.** Rectangle or rounded rectangle for the cell body. Numbered process stages inside, read left-to-right. Inputs (dendrites) enter from the left edge as 2-5 lines of varying weight. Output (axon) exits to the right with a terminal bulb. Plastic surfaces (memory, weights) listed below the cell as labeled blocks with cadence tags ("updates: every turn", "updates: nightly"). Do NOT render anatomical detail unless it carries information.

**4.2 Brain region map.** Stylized profile silhouette. Color-fill each region with its semantic color from §3. Do NOT render gyri/sulci texture as procedural noise — adds nothing and crowds. Real anatomical detail (e.g. seahorse-shape Hippocampus) helps when the region's name is anatomical; otherwise schematic ovals are clearer.
